`hmac.compare_digest(a, b)` is the helper function in the `hmac` module for comparing digests. The docs recommend it over `==` when checking a digest against an externally supplied one, to reduce the risk of timing attacks.

`secrets.compare_digest(a, b)` is the matching function in `secrets`. It uses a "constant-time compare" and points to `hmac.compare_digest` for further details.

I did not open the full `compare_digest` entry in `library/hmac.rst`, so the "no content-based short-circuiting" wording comes from the constant-time and timing-attack descriptions in the snippets.
